title: The Spark and Grove borrow subsidy decays linearly from SOFR to the Base Rate over twenty-four months
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.2.1 entitles both Spark and Grove to borrow up to one billion USDS "at a subsidized rate for an initial period of 2 years, beginning January 1, 2026." A.2.8.2.2.2.2.2 gives the formula: `SOFR + ((Base_Rate - SOFR) * T/24)`, where T counts elapsed months and "is equal to zero (0) for the first month."

At T=0 the Prime pays SOFR — the risk-free benchmark, a deep subsidy. At T=24 the term equals the full gap, so the rate is the Base Rate and the subsidy is gone. In between it closes linearly, one twenty-fourth of the gap per month.

A glide path rather than a cliff is the substantive choice. A subsidy that expires at a date forces a Prime's economics to change discontinuously, which either strands positions that were viable only at the concessionary rate or invites lobbying for extension as the date nears. Monthly convergence makes every position's viability decay gradually, so the Prime can adjust continuously and the ecosystem can observe whether it is doing so.

Anchoring the floor to SOFR rather than to a fixed number keeps the subsidy meaningful across rate environments — it always means "the risk-free rate," not a stale number that could become punitive or free depending on markets.

The reference point at the other end also moves: A.2.8.2.2.2.2.3 makes the Base Rate "dynamic and aligned with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate)," so a Prime ultimately pays roughly what Sky pays its own savers. Sky is therefore lending near its cost of funds rather than at a profit margin, and its return on Primes comes from the settlement mechanics instead.
description: The rate is SOFR plus the gap to the Base Rate scaled by elapsed months over 24, starting at zero, so the subsidy is fully retired on a schedule rather than at a cliff.
